officialTitle: Alectinib versus Crizotinib in Untreated ALK-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: we randomly assigned 303 patients with previously untreated, advanced ALK-positive NSCLC to receive either alectinib (600 mg twice daily) or crizotinib (250 mg twice daily)
design.notes: Patients with asymptomatic CNS disease were eligible.

clinicalQuestion: Is the CNS-penetrant ALK inhibitor alectinib superior to crizotinib as first-line therapy for advanced ALK-positive NSCLC?

pico.population: Previously untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC, including asymptomatic CNS disease
pico.outcomes: Primary: investigator-assessed PFS. Secondary: IRC PFS, time to CNS progression, ORR, OS

arms.label: Alectinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive either alectinib (600 mg twice daily)

publications.title: Alectinib versus Crizotinib in Untreated ALK-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

publications.title: Alectinib versus crizotinib in previously untreated ALK-positive advanced non-small cell lung cancer: final overall survival analysis of the phase III ALEX study.
publications.label: Final overall survival analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The rate of investigator-assessed progression-free survival was significantly higher with alectinib than with crizotinib (12-month event-free survival rate, 68.4% [95% confidence interval (CI), 61.0 to 75.9] with alectinib vs. 48.7% [95% CI, 40.4 to 56.9] with crizotinib; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.34 to 0.65]; P<0.001); the median progression-free survival with alectinib was not reached.

A total of 18 patients (12%) in the alectinib group had an event of CNS progression, as compared with 68 patients (45%) in the crizotinib group (cause-specific hazard ratio, 0.16; 95% CI, 0.10 to 0.28; P<0.001).

A response occurred in 126 patients in the alectinib group (response rate, 82.9%; 95% CI, 76.0 to 88.5) and in 114 patients in the crizotinib group (response rate, 75.5%; 95% CI, 67.8 to 82.1) (P=0.09).

At the updated data cut-off (28 April 2025), after a median follow-up of 53.5 (alectinib) and 23.3 (crizotinib) months, median OS was 81.1 [95% confidence interval (CI) 62.3 months-not estimable] versus 54.2 (95% CI 34.6-75.6 months) months, respectively [hazard ratio (HR) 0.78; 95% CI 0.56-1.08].
Median DOR in confirmed responders was longer with alectinib (42.3 months, 95% CI 31.3-51.3 months) versus crizotinib [11.1 months, 95% CI 7.9-13.0 months (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.30-0.56)].

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 to 5 adverse events were less frequent with alectinib (41% vs. 50% with crizotinib).

strengths: Randomised phase III including patients with asymptomatic CNS metastases
Mature final OS analysis with long follow-up
limitations: Final OS HR confidence interval crosses 1

clinicalImplications.text: Established alectinib as a first-line standard for advanced ALK-positive NSCLC, with marked reduction in CNS progression versus crizotinib.

tumourBoardPearl.text: CNS protection is a key differentiator of next-generation ALK TKIs over crizotinib.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 28586279 (primary) and PMID 41110693 (final OS).
